name: BambooHR
subcategory: HR, recruiting, payroll and workforce operations
tagline: Maintain a private employee directory, documents, and leave approvals

pricing.notes: Pricing is sales-led; canonical monthly amount is null.

tiers.name: Core
tiers.limits: Starts at $10/employee/month; 1 compliance course; core HR records, reporting, hiring, onboarding, time off, and employee experience
tiers.notes: Organizations with 25 or fewer employees pay a flat minimum starting at $250/month.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Starts at $17/employee/month; 15 compliance courses; adds performance and expanded employee-experience features
tiers.notes: Organizations with 25 or fewer employees pay a flat minimum starting at $250/month.

tiers.name: Elite
tiers.limits: Starts at $25/employee/month; 300+ compliance courses; 2 hours/year data-integrity support; 2 admin sessions/year; 30 additional implementation days
tiers.notes: Organizations with 25 or fewer employees pay a flat minimum starting at $250/month.

pricing.billingTerms: published monthly starting rates; extended/annual contracts are quote-only
pricing.hiddenCosts: Teams of 25 or fewer face a $250/month minimum instead of simple per-seat multiplication. Payroll, Benefits Administration, Time Tracking, and Global Employment are separate add-ons.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For BambooHR, maintain a private employee directory, documents, and leave approvals. The hard boundary is hr workflows, payroll integrations, benefits, compliance, reporting, and support, plus compliance, payroll, and regulated integrations.
coreLoopDIY: Track non-sensitive people operations in a private employee directory with documents, maintain leave approvals and records, and export data without calculating payroll or making employment decisions.
whatYouLose: HR workflows, payroll integrations, benefits, compliance, reporting, and support
identity checks and global employment infrastructure
ongoingBurden: sensitive data, access, retention, audit, payroll calculations, filings, benefits, employment law, incident response, and support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for BambooHR because HR platforms survive because mistakes affect pay, benefits, immigration, and legal obligations, not because forms are difficult to render. The recurring cost buys sensitive data, access, retention, audit, payroll calculations, filings, benefits, employment law, incident response, and support, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Frappe HR
priorArt.desc: Active open-source human-resources and payroll application built on Frappe.

alternatives.name: Connecteam Small Business Plan
alternatives.desc: Directory, documents, leave and onboarding for ten people; employee eleven is the business model.

facts.install: Hosted signup, then invite staff to the web and mobile apps
facts.dataFormat: Employee records, documents, schedules and time data in Connecteam's cloud; schedules and timesheets export to Excel, PDF, CSV or payroll-specific files
facts.gapVsPaid: The ten-user ceiling and frontline-operations focus leave it shallower than BambooHR's employee-record and reporting system.

alternatives.name: OrangeHRM Starter
alternatives.desc: The old-school HR suite: records, leave, attendance and approvals, with a real server and no fashion budget.

facts.install: Use the free hosted Starter signup, or upload the release to an Apache/PHP/MySQL server and complete the web installer
facts.dataFormat: Hosted Starter keeps employee records in OrangeHRM's cloud; self-hosted Starter stores them in MySQL/MariaDB with uploaded files in application storage
facts.gapVsPaid: Its older interface and smaller integration/reporting ecosystem are a step down from BambooHR, especially when self-hosted.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting requires Apache, PHP and MySQL/MariaDB plus security and backups; the hosted path starts with a 30-day trial before conversion to lifetime-free Starter

alternatives.name: Horilla HR
alternatives.desc: Hire-to-leave HR in Docker; free forever means you own the updates and backups.

facts.install: Clone the stable 2.0 branch and run docker-compose up -d; a manual Django setup is also documented
facts.dataFormat: HR records in PostgreSQL by default, with uploaded media on server storage or optional Google Cloud Storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It is younger and less polished than BambooHR, with server operations and upgrades shifted to the user.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker and production configuration: database credentials, secret key, allowed hosts, HTTPS, backups and mail remain the operator's job

alternatives.name: Frappe HR
alternatives.desc: A complete HR suite without the license bill; the server, backups and upgrades are now in your job description.

facts.install: Launch its Docker Compose stack, or install hrms and ERPNext into an existing Frappe Bench
facts.dataFormat: Each Frappe site has its own MariaDB database plus private/public files directories; backups are SQL dumps and file archives under the site
facts.gapVsPaid: The broad Frappe/ERP stack is much harder to operate and less streamlined than BambooHR's managed HRIS.
facts.setupBlocker: The full Frappe/ERPNext stack brings Docker, MariaDB, Redis, proxy/TLS and version-compatible app upgrades

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Core plan and a internal records tracker without payroll DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for BambooHR in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: track non-sensitive people operations in a private employee directory with documents, maintain leave approvals and records, and export data without calculating payroll or making employment decisions.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement employees, teams, roles, documents, leave requests, equipment, onboarding tasks, and acknowledgements.
Use least-privilege roles and log every read or change to sensitive records.
Add approval workflows, expiry reminders, export, retention, deletion holds, and encrypted backups.
Keep compensation fields optional and never calculate payroll, taxes, benefits, or statutory filings.
Provide a data dictionary and explain which fields should not be stored without legal review.
Ship Docker Compose, health checks, disaster recovery, and an emergency-access procedure.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out payroll calculation or money movement.
Deliberately leave out automated hiring decisions or applicant scoring.
Deliberately leave out tax, benefits, immigration, identity, and global-employment compliance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
